subject: Optimization algorithm for FIML with missing data

messages.author: 74d8604b3526e22e
messages.subject: Optimization algorithm for FIML with missing data
parts:
May I ask some questions about the fitting algorithm?


If I use fit the following model to data with missing,
 cfa( model , data= missing.data ,meanstructure = TRUE, missing = "FIML")

what kind of optimization algorithm the lavaan package will use ?
EM, quasi-Newton, gradient-only + quasi-Newton or Gauss-Newton?  does it use the normal likelihood or Wishart likelihood?


I saw in some slides:

"fit the model with full-information maximum likelihood; if you switch on the verbose=TRUE option, you can see how the EM algorithm is used to estimate the (unrestricted) mean vector and covariance matrix of the data, in the presence of missing data."

Thank you very much!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Optimization algorithm for FIML with missing data
parts:
On 11/16/2013 12:32 AM, Chen Tuki wrote:
> May I ask some questions about the fitting algorithm?
>
>
> If I use fit the following model to data with missing,
> cfa( model , data= missing.data ,meanstructure = TRUE, missing = "FIML")
>
> what kind of optimization algorithm the lavaan package will use ?
> EM, quasi-Newton, gradient-only + quasi-Newton or Gauss-Newton? does it
> use the normal likelihood or Wishart likelihood?

To estimate the parameters of the model (in the presence of missing
data), lavaan uses the same optimization algorithm as in the complete
case: quasi-newton (using the nlminb() optimizer). We just use a
different objective function that needs to be minimzed (see
lav_objective.R in the source code).

The EM algorithm is NOT used for estimating the free parameters (in this
case). It is only used to estimate the (sample-based) covariance matrix
and mean vector. This corresponds to the 'unrestricted' model. We only
need this to compute the LRT (the model chi-square test statistic),
since this is just comparing the user-specified (restricted or h0) model
versus the unrestricted (h1) model.

Hope this helps,

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Optimization algorithm for FIML with missing data
parts:
On 11/17/2013 05:33 AM, Chen Tuki wrote:
> Thank you very much! That's very helpful.
> May I ask one more question?
>
> The algorithm did not converge for some of my data sets.
> How can I change default maximum number of iterations to see if that
> helps the convergence?

By using the 'control' argument. You can change all the control
parameters of the nlminb() function using this argument. See ?nlminb for
an overview.

Changing the default maximum number of iterations can be done like this:

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, control=list(iter.max=5))

But the default number is already very high (10000). You may want to
relax the stopping criteria. In particular, the rel.tol and abs.tol
values. The latter is only relevant if you have a saturated model, and
the mimimum of the objective function is zero (as in a regression
model). The default value of rel.tol is 1e-10. To relax this, you can try eg

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
control=list(rel.tol=1e-8), verbose=TRUE)

Yves.
